Yes. The subtext enriches the setting rather than feeling forced. Bureaucratic phrases such as “localized moisture condition” and “microbial growth” imply an institution managing responsibility and appearances alongside the actual damage. Faculty adopting those euphemisms shows how institutional language gradually shapes everyday life.

The recurring blue-bird saucer also quietly contrasts domestic care with systemic neglect: Vale can catch the drops, but she cannot fix the building. These details make Barlow more than a deteriorating workplace; it becomes a setting defined by uncertainty, accommodation, and the persistence of teaching despite eroded trust.
